title: Homemade Sausage Rolls with Wedges & Beans

steps.title: Prep the veg and pastry
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into wedges and finely chop the red onion. Unroll the pastry, cut it in half widthways, then wrap and chill (or freeze) the spare half. Cut the remaining piece in half lengthways to make two long strips.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a small frying pan over a medium-low heat. Cook the onion for 8–10 min, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly golden. Tip onto a plate to cool.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Toss the wedges on a large baking tray with 1½ tbsp oil, the smoked paprika (optional) and a pinch of salt. Roast on the top shelf for 35–40 min, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: While the wedges roast, slit the sausage skins and squeeze the meat into a bowl. Add the cooled onion, panko, mixed herbs and a pinch of pepper. Mix well with your hands.

steps.title: Roll the sausage rolls
steps.text: Shape the filling into two long sausages and lay one along the middle of each pastry strip. Brush one long edge with egg, fold the pastry over and press the join with a fork to seal. Cut each into 3 rolls, put on a lined baking tray, brush with egg and snip two small slits in the tops.

steps.title: Bake the sausage rolls
steps.text: Bake on the shelf below the wedges for 22–25 min until puffed and deep golden. The sausagemeat should be piping hot with no pink in the middle.

steps.title: Heat the beans and serve
steps.text: For the last 5 min, warm the beans in a small pan over a medium heat, stirring, until bubbling. Serve the sausage rolls with the wedges, beans and ketchup (optional).

title: Roast Pork with Crackling, Roasties & Apple Sauce

ingredients.t: 1 small crackling joint (about 700g); leftovers make great sandwiches
2 tsp for the rind, plus extra

steps.title: Prep the pork and veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan). Pat the pork rind really dry with kitchen paper. Peel and halve the potatoes, halve the carrots lengthways and cut the broccoli into florets. Halve the onion, and peel, core and chop the apples.

steps.title: Start the pork
steps.text: Rub the meat (not the rind) with 1 tsp oil, the fennel seeds (optional) and pepper. Rub the rind with 1 tsp oil, then 2 tsp salt, working it into the scores. Sit it rind-side up on the onion halves in a roasting tin. Roast on the top shelf for 25 min, until the rind starts to bubble.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in a pan of salted water for 8 min. Drain, leave to steam for 2 min, then shake in the colander to rough up the edges. Toss the carrots with 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Roast low and slow
steps.text: After 25 min, turn the oven down to 200°C (180°C fan) and pour 100ml water into the pork tin, keeping the rind dry. Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a second tray for 5 min, tip in the potatoes and carrots and turn to coat. Roast both for 45–50 min, turning the veg once, until the pork juices run clear when the thickest part is pierced.

steps.title: Rest and crisp up
steps.text: Lift the pork onto a board and rest, uncovered, for 15 min (foil softens the crackling). Turn the oven up to 220°C (200°C fan) and give the potatoes and carrots 15 min more until crunchy. If any crackling is still chewy, slice it off and crisp it on the potato tray.

steps.title: Make the apple sauce
steps.text: While the pork rests, put the apples, butter and 2 tbsp water in a small covered pan over a medium-low heat. Cook for 8–10 min until the apples collapse, then mash with a fork and stir in the honey (optional).

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Spoon the fat off the pork tin, add 300ml boiling water and scrape up the sticky bits. Strain into a small saucepan, pressing the onion. Whisk in the gravy granules over a medium heat and simmer for 1–2 min until thick.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli and serve
steps.text: For the last 4 min, boil the broccoli in salted water until just tender, then drain. Carve the pork into thick slices and break up the crackling. Serve with the roasties, carrots, broccoli, apple sauce and gravy poured beside (not over) the crackling.

title: Steak & Ale Pie with Buttery Mash & Broccoli

steps.title: Prep the filling
steps.text: Chop the onion, cut the carrot into chunks and crush the garlic. Dissolve the stock cube in 200ml boiling water. Toss the beef with the flour, a pinch of salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oil in a casserole or deep lidded pan over a high heat. Brown the beef in two batches for 4–5 min each, until deep brown all over. Lift onto a plate; the brown bits in the pan are flavour.

steps.title: Simmer the filling
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium, add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 min. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 min, then pour in the ale, scraping the bottom. Add the stock, Worcestershire, mixed herbs (optional) and beef. Cover and simmer over a low heat for 1½ hours, stirring now and then. It is ready when the beef is tender and the gravy coats a spoon.

steps.title: Top the pie
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spoon the filling into a small pie dish (about 1 litre) and leave to cool for 10 min. Brush the rim with egg, lay the pastry over and press the edges to seal, then trim. Brush with egg and cut a small hole in the middle for steam.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.text: Put the pie on a baking tray and bake on the middle shelf for 25–30 min until puffed, deep golden and bubbling at the edges.

steps.title: Make the mash
steps.text: While the pie bakes, boil the potatoes in a large pan of salted water for 15 min until tender. Drain, leave to steam for 2 min, then mash with the butter, milk and a pinch of salt until smooth.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli and serve
steps.text: For the last 4 min, boil the broccoli in salted water until just tender, then drain. Serve the pie with a big spoonful of mash, the broccoli and extra gravy from the dish.

title: Lancashire Hotpot with a Crispy Sliced Potato Top

ingredients.t: 1 lamb or beef cube in 350ml boiling water

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Slice the onions and carrot, and thinly slice the potatoes to about 3mm. Dissolve the stock cube in 350ml boiling water and melt the butter.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Toss the lamb with the mixed herbs, salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a flameproof casserole (or a frying pan) over a high heat. Brown the lamb for 4–5 min until coloured all over. Lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and cook the onions and carrot for 8–10 min until soft and golden. Stir in the flour for 1 min, then gradually stir in the stock and Worcestershire until it thickens. Return the lamb and season.

steps.title: Layer the potatoes
steps.text: If you used a frying pan, tip everything into a small ovenproof dish (about 1 litre). Lay the potato slices over the top, overlapping like roof tiles. Brush with half the melted butter and season.

steps.title: Bake covered
steps.text: Cover with a lid or foil and bake on the middle shelf for 1 hour 15 min, until the lamb is tender.

steps.title: Crisp the top
steps.text: Uncover, brush the potatoes with the remaining butter and turn the oven up to 200°C (180°C fan). Bake for 35–40 min more until the top is golden and crisp at the edges and a knife slides easily through the potatoes.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli and serve
steps.text: For the last 4 min, boil the broccoli in salted water until just tender, then drain. Leave the hotpot to settle for a couple of minutes, then serve with the broccoli.

title: Chicken & Chorizo Traybake with Crispy Potatoes

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into 3cm chunks, the pepper into chunks and the red onion into wedges. Cut the chorizo into chunks and bash the garlic cloves.

steps.title: Start the potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes in a large roasting tray with 1 tbsp oil, half the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast on the top shelf for 15 min to get a head start.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: While the potatoes roast, toss the chicken in a bowl with the remaining oil and paprika. Add the mixed herbs (optional), salt and pepper.

steps.title: Roast the chicken and chorizo
steps.text: Add the chicken, chorizo, pepper, onion and garlic to the tray and turn everything in the oil, sitting the chicken on top. Roast for 25 min, until the chicken is starting to brown and the chorizo releases its red oil.

steps.title: Add the tomatoes
steps.text: Scatter over the tomatoes and roast for 8–10 min more, until they burst and the potatoes are crisp. The chicken should be golden and cooked through, with no pink and clear juices.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach and serve
steps.text: Take the tray out and stir the spinach through the hot juices for 1–2 min until wilted. Drizzle with the honey (optional) and serve straight from the tray.

title: Crispy Corned Beef Hash with Fried Eggs

ingredients.swap: Scatter the spring onions over one plate only.

ingredients.t: a pinch, plus extra for the potato water

steps.title: Prep the hash
steps.text: Put the kettle on. Cut the potatoes into 2cm cubes, slice the red onion and crush the garlic. Cut the corned beef into 2cm chunks (chilling the tin first helps it slice neatly). Slice the spring onions (optional).

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: Boil the potatoes in a pan of salted water for 5–6 min until just tender at the edges. Drain and leave to steam dry for 2 min.

steps.title: Brown the corned beef
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the corned beef for 3–4 min until crisp at the edges, then lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add another 1 tsp oil and cook the onion over a medium heat for 5 min until soft. Stir in the garlic, mustard and Worcestershire for 1 min.

steps.title: Crisp the hash
steps.text: Add the remaining oil and the potatoes and press them down. Fry for 10–12 min, turning only every 3 min so a golden crust forms. Fold the corned beef back in and season with pepper; it is salty, so taste before adding salt.

steps.title: Cook the eggs and serve
steps.text: Make 4 hollows in the hash and crack an egg into each. Cover with a lid or baking tray and cook over a medium-low heat for 3–4 min until the whites are set. Scatter with the spring onions (optional) and serve from the pan.

title: Honey-Garlic Lamb Chops with Buttery New Potatoes

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Boil a full kettle and heat the grill to high. Halve any larger potatoes so they're all a similar size, and cut the broccoli into florets. Peel the garlic: halve one clove and crush the other. In a small bowl, mix the honey with the mixed herbs and a pinch of salt and pepper.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a medium saucepan, cover with boiling water from the kettle and add a pinch of salt. Simmer over a medium-high heat for 15–18 min, until a knife slides in easily.

steps.title: Grill the lamb chops
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, rub the chops all over with the cut side of the halved garlic clove. Rub with the oil and season with salt and pepper. Grill on a rack for 3–4 min each side for pink, or 5 min each side for well done.

steps.title: Glaze and rest the lamb
steps.text: Brush the honey glaze over the chops and grill for a final 1 min, until sticky and golden at the edges. Move to a warm plate and rest for 3 min.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli
steps.text: When the potatoes have 4 min left, add the broccoli to the same pan. Cook until bright green and just tender.

steps.title: Butter the potatoes
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and broccoli well and return them to the pan off the heat. Add the butter, the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt and pepper. Toss gently until the butter melts and coats everything.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Pile the buttery potatoes and broccoli onto plates and add two chops each. Spoon over any resting juices and serve with the lemon wedges (optional).

title: Roast Sirloin of Beef with Yorkshires, Roasties & Gravy

steps.title: Prep and make the batter
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and boil a full kettle. Peel the potatoes and cut into large chunks; cut the carrots into batons and the broccoli into florets. Take the steaks out of the fridge. Whisk the flour, egg and a pinch of salt in a jug, then whisk in the milk until smooth and leave to rest.

steps.title: Par-boil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with boiling water in a saucepan, add a pinch of salt and boil for 8 min. Meanwhile, put 2 tbsp oil in a roasting tin and heat in the oven for 5 min. Drain the potatoes, leave to steam for 2 min, then shake in the colander to rough up the edges.

steps.title: Roast the potatoes
steps.text: Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil and turn to coat. Season and roast on the middle shelf for 45–50 min, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Sear and roast the beef
steps.text: When the potatoes have been in for 15 min, rub the steaks with 2 tsp oil, the coarse pepper and a pinch of salt. Sear in an ovenproof frying pan over a high heat for 1½ min each side, then hold the fat edge down for 30 sec. Roast in the oven for 6 min for medium-rare (8 min for medium). Rest on a board under foil for at least 15 min.

steps.title: Bake the Yorkshires
steps.text: Straight after the beef comes out, put ½ tsp oil into each of 4 holes of a muffin tin. Heat on the top shelf for 5 min, until smoking hot. Quickly pour in the batter and bake for 18–20 min, until puffed and deep golden. Don't open the oven door for the first 15 min.

steps.title: Cook the veg
steps.text: While the Yorkshires bake, boil the carrots in a pan of salted water over a medium-high heat for 4 min. Add the broccoli and cook for 4 min more, until both are just tender. Drain.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Stir the gravy granules into 250ml boiling water from the kettle until smooth and thickened. Pour in any juices from the resting beef.

steps.title: Carve and serve
steps.text: Slice the beef thinly across the grain. Share it between plates with the roast potatoes, Yorkshires and veg, then pour over the hot gravy. Add a spoonful of mustard on the side (optional).

title: Crispy Prawn Scampi & Chips with Tartare Sauce

ingredients.swap: Leave it out of the flour and sprinkle a pinch over one portion's scampi after frying instead.

ingredients.t: 1½ tbsp for the chips, plus about 100ml for shallow-frying
1: zest, juice of half, rest in wedges

ingredients.swap: Spoon one portion of the lemony mayo into a separate dish before stirring in the gherkins.
Stir the capers into one portion of the tartare only.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the potatoes into chunky chips, rinse, then pat them and the defrosted prawns really dry. Zest the lemon, juice one half and cut the rest into wedges. Finely chop the gherkins and capers (optional).

steps.title: Roast the chips
steps.text: Toss the chips on a large baking tray with 1½ tbsp oil and a good pinch of salt. Spread out in one layer. Roast on the top shelf for 35–40 min, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Make the tartare sauce
steps.text: While the chips roast, mix the mayonnaise with a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of pepper. Stir in the gherkins and capers (optional). Chill until needed.

steps.title: Crumb the prawns
steps.text: When the chips have 15 min left, set out three plates. Season the flour with salt, pepper and chilli powder (optional) on the first. Beat the egg on the second, and mix the panko with the lemon zest on the third. Dust each prawn in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the crumbs.

steps.title: Fry the scampi
steps.text: Heat about 100ml oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat until a crumb sizzles straight away. Fry half the prawns for 1½–2 min each side, until the crumb is golden and the prawns are pink and opaque all the way through. Drain on kitchen paper and repeat. Let the leftover oil cool before throwing it away.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Pile the chips onto plates with a sprinkle of salt and add the scampi. Serve with a pot of tartare sauce and the lemon wedges for squeezing.

title: Peri-Peri Chicken Thighs with Spicy Rice & Peri Mayo

ingredients.swap: Make the marinade without the chilli flakes, coat all the chicken, then rub the flakes onto one portion's thighs only.

ingredients.t: 1: juice of half, rest in wedges
1 chicken stock cube in 300ml boiling water

ingredients.swap: Leave it out of the pan; warm the sweetcorn separately (1 min in the microwave) and stir it into one portion only.
Stir the hot sauce into half the mayo only and leave the rest plain.
Scatter over one plate only.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Boil the kettle and make up 300ml stock with the cube. Finely chop the onion, dice the pepper into 1cm pieces and crush the garlic. Juice half the lemon and cut the rest into wedges. Slice the spring onions (optional).

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the paprika, chilli flakes, herbs, honey, a third of the garlic, the lemon juice, 1 tbsp oil and the salt. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat well. Leave for 10 min while you start the pan (or overnight in the fridge).

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large, deep frying pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Brown the thighs for 3 min each side until coloured but not cooked through. Lift onto a plate, leaving the oil and marinade bits in the pan.

steps.title: Fry the veg and rice
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Fry the onion and pepper for 3 min until starting to soften, then add the rest of the garlic for 1 min. Stir in the rice and turmeric for 30 sec so every grain is coated and yellow.

steps.title: Simmer the rice and chicken
steps.text: Pour in the stock, add the sweetcorn and bring to a simmer. Sit the chicken thighs on top with any juices, cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 min without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Rest off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave covered for 10 min, until the rice is tender and the stock absorbed. Cut into the thickest thigh to check there's no pink and the juices run clear.

steps.title: Make the peri mayo
steps.text: While the rice rests, stir the hot sauce into the mayonnaise (optional). Add a squeeze of lemon from one wedge and mix well.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Lift off the chicken, fluff up the rice with a fork and spoon into bowls. Top with the thighs, drizzle with peri mayo and scatter over the spring onions (optional). Serve with the remaining lemon wedges.

title: Crispy-Skin Sea Bass, New Potatoes & Cucumber Relish

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the salad without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.

steps.title: Prep the relish veg
steps.text: Boil a full kettle. Peel the cucumber, then shave it into long ribbons with a vegetable peeler, stopping at the seedy core. Thinly slice the red onion, then toss both with a pinch of salt in a sieve for 10 min to draw out the water. Quarter the potatoes and separate the little gem leaves.

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with boiling water and add a pinch of salt. Simmer over a medium-high heat for 12–15 min, until a knife slides through easily.

steps.title: Dress the relish
steps.text: While the potatoes cook, squeeze the cucumber and onion firmly, rinse under cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper. In a bowl, mix the rice vinegar with the honey (optional) until dissolved. Stir three-quarters of this into the cucumber and onion; keep the rest for the salad.

steps.title: Fry the sea bass
steps.text: Pat the fish skin dry, make 2–3 shallow cuts in it and heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Lay the fillets in skin-side down, pressing flat with a spatula for 30 sec. Season the flesh and cook for 3–4 min, until the skin is crisp and the flesh is nearly opaque. Flip, turn off the heat and leave for 1 min.

steps.title: Butter the potatoes
steps.text: Drain the potatoes and return to the pan off the heat. Toss with the butter and a pinch of salt and pepper until glossy.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Toss the little gem with the rest of the dressing and 1 tsp oil. Share the potatoes between plates and top with the sea bass, skin-side up. Add a heap of cucumber relish, the salad and the lemon wedges (optional).

title: Creamy Beef Stroganoff with Fluffy Rice

ingredients.t: 1 tsp, plus a pinch to serve
½ beef stock cube in 100ml boiling water

ingredients.swap: Scatter over one plate only.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Boil the kettle and make up 100ml stock with the half cube. Thinly slice the onion and crush the garlic. Trim the fat from the steak, slice it across the grain into 1cm strips and season with salt and pepper. Slice the spring onion (optional).

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice, put it in a saucepan with 300ml boiling water and a pinch of salt, and bring back to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 10–12 min. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 min.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: While the rice cooks, heat the butter and ½ tbsp oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat until foaming. Cook the onion for 6–8 min, stirring often, until soft and golden. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 min, then tip into a bowl.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Turn the heat to high and add the remaining ½ tbsp oil. Lay the steak strips in a single layer and cook for 1 min, then turn and cook for 30 sec more. They should still be pink inside; tip them into the bowl with the onion.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Pour the stock into the pan with the mustard and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up the browned bits. Bubble for 1–2 min until reduced by half. Turn the heat to low and stir in the soured cream until smooth and hot; don't let it boil or it may split.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.text: Return the steak, onion and any juices to the pan. Stir gently over a low heat for 1 min, just until the beef is hot through. Taste and season.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fluff up the rice with a fork and share between bowls. Spoon over the stroganoff, then finish with a pinch of paprika and the spring onion (optional).

title: Chicken, Leek & Carrot Casserole with Garlic Mash

ingredients.t: 1 chicken stock cube in 400ml boiling water

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Boil a full kettle and make up 400ml stock with the cube. Chop the onion, cut the carrots into thick rounds, and halve, rinse and slice the leek. Crush 1 garlic clove; peel the other 3 and leave whole. Halve the chicken thighs and season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan or casserole with a lid over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 3–4 min each side until golden all over (it will finish cooking later). Lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrots and leek to the pan and cook for 5 min, stirring, until starting to soften. Stir in the crushed garlic, tomato purée and mixed herbs for 1 min.

steps.title: Simmer the casserole
steps.text: Pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken and its juices and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 35 min, until the chicken is tender and the carrots are soft.

steps.title: Make the garlic mash
steps.text: While the casserole simmers, peel the potatoes and cut into even chunks. Boil with the 3 whole garlic cloves in salted water over a medium-high heat for 15–20 min, until soft. Drain, then mash the potatoes and garlic with the butter and milk until smooth. Season and keep covered.

steps.title: Thicken the gravy
steps.text: Mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp cold water until smooth. Stir it into the casserole and simmer uncovered for 3–5 min, until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. Check a piece of chicken has no pink, then taste and season.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Spoon the garlic mash into shallow bowls. Ladle the chicken casserole and its gravy alongside.

title: Full English Fry-Up with Sausages, Bacon & Eggs

ingredients.swap: Leave the tomatoes off one plate.
Roast the mushrooms on their own small tray (or a separate corner lined with foil) and serve them on one plate only.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Halve the cherry tomatoes and the mushrooms (optional). Line a baking tray with foil.

steps.title: Roast the sausages
steps.text: Spread the sausages out in a small roasting tin, without pricking them. Roast on the top shelf for 30 min in total, turning halfway, until browned all over and cooked through.

steps.title: Roast the tomatoes
steps.text: After the sausages have had 10 min, lay the tomatoes cut-side up on one half of the lined tray. Put the mushrooms (optional) in their own corner. Drizzle with half the oil and sprinkle with the herbs (optional), salt and pepper. Roast on the middle shelf for 20 min, until soft and juicy.

steps.title: Bake the bacon
steps.text: When the sausages have 12 min left, lay the bacon on the free half of the tray. Bake for 10–12 min, until cooked through and the fat is golden at the edges.

steps.title: Warm the beans
steps.text: While the bacon cooks, tip the beans into a small saucepan. Heat over a medium-low heat for 4–5 min, stirring now and then, until bubbling.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 min, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Meanwhile, toast the bread and spread with the butter.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Share everything between warm plates: sausages, bacon, an egg, tomatoes, beans and buttered toast. Serve with ketchup (optional).

title: Slow-Cooker Lamb Shanks with Rich Gravy & Mash

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.text: Boil the kettle and make up 450ml stock with the cube. Finely chop the onion, cut the carrots into small chunks and crush the garlic. Season the lamb shanks all over with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Brown the shanks for 8–10 min, turning, until well coloured on all sides. Move them into the slow cooker.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Turn the heat under the same pan to medium. Cook the onion and carrots for 5 min, stirring, until softened, then add the garlic for 1 min. Stir in the stock, tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce and mixed herbs, scraping up the browned bits, and bring to a simmer. Pour over the lamb.

steps.title: Slow-cook the lamb
steps.text: Cover and cook on low for 7–8 hours, until the meat is meltingly tender and pulls away from the bone. No slow cooker? Cook in a lidded casserole in the oven at 180°C (160°C fan) for 3–3½ hours instead. Add a splash of water in the last hour if it looks dry.

steps.title: Make the mash
steps.text: About 30 min before the lamb is ready, peel the potatoes and cut into even chunks. Boil in salted water over a medium-high heat for 15–20 min, until soft. Drain, then mash with the butter and milk until smooth. Season and keep covered.

steps.title: Thicken the gravy
steps.text: Lift the shanks onto a plate and cover with foil. Pour the sauce and veg into a saucepan, stir in the honey and bring to a bubble over a medium heat. Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water, then whisk it in gradually and simmer for 2–3 min, until the gravy coats a spoon. Season.

steps.title: Cook the broccoli
steps.text: While the gravy bubbles, cook the broccoli in a pan of boiling salted water for 3–4 min, until just tender. Drain.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Spoon the mash onto warm plates and sit a lamb shank on top of each. Pour over plenty of gravy with its carrots and serve the broccoli on the side.

title: Quiche Lorraine with Mustard Potato Salad

ingredients.swap: Keep the spring onions in a small bowl and stir them into one portion of potato salad only.

steps.title: Get prepped
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan and put a baking tray in to heat. Take the pastry out of the fridge 10 min before unrolling so it doesn't crack. Finely chop the onion, crush the garlic and cut the bacon into thin strips. Grate the cheddar.

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Unroll the pastry and press it into a 20cm loose-bottomed tart tin, letting the excess hang over the edge. Prick the base all over with a fork. Line with scrunched-up baking paper and fill with baking beans or uncooked rice.

steps.title: Blind-bake the case
steps.text: Bake on the hot tray for 15 min until the edges are set. Lift out the paper and beans, then bake for 8–10 min more until the base looks dry and pale golden. Trim the overhanging pastry with a sharp knife.

steps.title: Fry the bacon
steps.text: While the case bakes, melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the bacon, onion and garlic for 6–8 min until the bacon is light golden and the onion is soft. Tip onto kitchen paper to drain and cool a little.

steps.title: Fill and bake the quiche
steps.text: Whisk the eggs and cream in a jug with a good grind of black pepper; the bacon brings enough salt. Scatter the bacon mixture over the pastry case, then the cheddar. Pour in the egg mix and push some filling under the surface. Bake for 30–35 min until golden on top with a slight wobble in the centre.

steps.title: Cook the potatoes

title: Lamb Keema Curry with Spiced Potatoes & Warm Naan

ingredients.t: 1 chicken or lamb cube in 250ml water

ingredients.swap: Keep the coriander in a little bowl on the table so it only goes on the plates that want it.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Boil the kettle. Cut the potato into 2cm chunks, leaving the skin on. Finely chop the onion and grate the garlic. Crumble the stock cube into 250ml just-boiled water and stir.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the lamb mince for 5–6 min, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned all over. Spoon away most of the fat, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan.

steps.title: Add the onion and spices
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium. Add the cumin seeds and onion and cook for 5 min until soft. Stir in the garlic, ginger paste, curry powder and turmeric and cook for 1 min until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer with the potatoes
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée, chopped tomatoes, potato and stock. Bring to a bubble, cover and simmer over a medium-low heat for 15–18 min, stirring now and then. It's ready when the potato is tender to the point of a knife and the sauce is thick.

steps.title: Warm the naan
steps.text: While the keema finishes, heat a dry frying pan over a medium heat. Flick a few drops of water over each naan and warm for 1 min each side until soft and lightly toasted. Wrap in a clean tea towel to keep warm.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir the spinach into the keema a handful at a time for 2 min until wilted. Add the garam masala and season with salt. Serve with the warm naan, a spoonful of yogurt (optional), mango chutney (optional) and coriander (optional).

title: One-Pot Chicken Pilau with Spinach & Cooling Raita

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the raita without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Keep the coriander in a little bowl on the table so it only goes on the plates that want it.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Boil the kettle. Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until it runs almost clear, then leave to drain. Thinly slice the onion, grate the carrot and garlic, and cut the chicken into 3cm chunks. Crumble the stock cube into 350ml just-boiled water.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide saucepan or casserole with a tight-fitting lid over a medium-high heat. Season the chicken with a pinch of salt and fry for 4–5 min, turning, until golden on most sides. It will finish cooking with the rice.

steps.title: Cook the onion and spices
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the butter, onion and carrot. Cook for 5–6 min, stirring, until the onion is soft and turning golden. Stir in the cumin seeds, garlic, ginger paste, garam masala and turmeric for 1 min until fragrant.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Stir in the drained rice until every grain is glossy and coated in spice. Pour in the hot stock, stir once and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 min without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Make the raita
steps.text: While the rice cooks, finely dice the cucumber. Stir it into the yogurt with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon (optional). Keep in the fridge until needed.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 10 min. For the last 3 min, quickly scatter the spinach on top and put the lid back on to wilt it. Fluff everything through with a fork and check the chicken is piping hot with no pink. Serve with the raita, lemon wedges (optional) and coriander (optional).

title: Chicken Tikka Kebabs in Naan with Garlic Yogurt Sauce

ingredients.t: 8 tbsp (2 for the marinade, 6 for the sauce)

ingredients.swap: Leave the onions off one plate.
Leave the lettuce off one plate.
Leave the cucumber off one plate.

ingredients.t: a knob, softened, for the naans

ingredients.swap: Serve the chilli sauce at the table so each person adds their own.
Keep the coriander in a little bowl on the table so it only goes on the kebabs that want it.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Cut the chicken into 3cm chunks. In a bowl, mix it with the tikka paste, 2 tbsp of the yogurt and the tomato purée until well coated. Leave for at least 15 min, or cover and chill for up to 24 hr.

steps.title: Pickle the onion
steps.text: Put the sliced red onion in a small bowl. Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon, add a big pinch of salt and scrunch together with your fingers. Leave to soften and turn pink while you do the rest.

steps.title: Prep the salad and sauce
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Shred the little gem, quarter the cherry tomatoes and thinly slice the cucumber. Stir the garlic, a squeeze from the other lemon half and a pinch of salt into the remaining 6 tbsp yogurt.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.text: Thread the chicken onto skewers, or spread it out on an oiled, foil-lined baking tray. Grill on the top shelf for 12–15 min, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink.

steps.title: Warm the naan
steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate and cover to keep warm. Spread the naans with the soft butter (optional) and grill for 1–2 min until puffed and lightly golden. Watch closely, as they catch quickly.

steps.title: Build the kebabs
steps.text: Lay each naan on a plate and pile on the lettuce, tomato, cucumber and chicken. Spoon over the garlic yogurt sauce and scatter with the pickled onion. Add chilli sauce (optional) and coriander (optional), then fold and eat.

title: Chicken Balti with Charred Peppers, Onion & Naan

ingredients.swap: Leave the chillies whole so they're easy to lift out, and spoon them onto one plate only.
Keep the coriander in a little bowl on the table so it only goes on the plates that want it.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Finely chop 1 onion and cut the remaining half into 2cm chunks. Cut the pepper into 2cm chunks, the chicken into bite-size pieces and grate the garlic. In a jug, mix the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, yogurt, ground coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and 1 tsp of the garam masala.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Heat 1½ tbsp oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over a medium heat. Add the cumin seeds for 30 sec until they sizzle, then the chopped onion. Cook for 10–12 min, stirring often, until deep golden; add a splash of water if it catches.

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger paste and green chillies (optional) for 1 min. Pour in the tomato mix and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook for 5 min, stirring, until thick and the oil starts to pool at the edges.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the masala. Pour in 100ml water, cover and cook over a low heat for 15 min, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Char the peppers
steps.text: While the chicken cooks, heat the remaining ½ tbsp oil in a second frying pan over a high heat. Fry the pepper and onion chunks for 4–5 min until charred at the edges but still with some bite.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir the peppers and onion into the curry and cook uncovered for 2–3 min, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce clings. Add the remaining garam masala, the lemon juice and salt to taste. Warm the naans in the pepper pan for 1 min each side and serve with coriander (optional).

title: Homemade Margherita Pizza with Fresh Basil

ingredients.swap: Scatter the basil over one pizza only, or serve it on the side.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the flour, yeast and ½ tsp salt. Add 160ml warm water and 1 tbsp oil and stir into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 min until smooth and springy.

steps.title: Prove the dough
steps.text: Put the dough back in the bowl, cover with a clean tea towel and leave somewhere warm for 30–45 min, until puffy and nearly doubled. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with two large baking trays inside.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Stir the garlic, mixed herbs, ½ tbsp oil and a pinch of salt and pepper into the passata. Tear the mozzarella into small pieces and pat dry with kitchen paper so the pizzas don't go soggy.

steps.title: Shape the bases
steps.text: Knock the air out of the dough and split it in two. On a floured surface, roll each piece into a thin round about 25cm across. Lay each one on a sheet of baking paper.

steps.title: Top the pizzas
steps.text: Spread half the sauce over each base, leaving a 1cm border. Scatter over the mozzarella and parmesan (optional). Drizzle with the remaining ½ tbsp oil.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Carefully slide each pizza, still on its paper, onto a hot tray. Bake for 10–12 min, until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling and spotted brown. Scatter with basil leaves (optional), slice and serve.

title: Homemade Ham & Pineapple Pizza with Melty Mozzarella

ingredients.swap: Sprinkle the chilli flakes over one pizza only, or put them on the table.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and ½ tsp salt in a large bowl. Pour in 160ml warm water and 1 tbsp oil and bring together into a soft, slightly tacky dough. Knead on a floured worktop for 8–10 min until it's smooth and springs back when pressed.

steps.title: Prove the dough
steps.text: Return the dough to the bowl and cover with a tea towel. Leave in a warm spot for 30–45 min, until puffed up and nearly doubled. While it rises, heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with two large baking trays inside.

steps.title: Prep the toppings
steps.text: Mix the passata with the garlic, mixed herbs, the remaining ½ tbsp oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Drain the pineapple well and pat dry with kitchen paper. Tear the ham into bite-size pieces, tear the mozzarella and grate the cheddar.

steps.title: Shape the bases
steps.text: Punch the dough down and cut it in half. Roll each half on a floured surface into a thin round about 25cm across. Lift each base onto its own sheet of baking paper.

steps.title: Top the pizzas
steps.text: Spread the sauce over the bases, leaving a 1cm border. Scatter over the mozzarella and cheddar. Dot the ham and pineapple evenly over the top.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Slide the pizzas on their paper onto the hot trays. Bake for 10–12 min, until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling. Sprinkle with chilli flakes (optional), cut into slices and serve.

title: Cheesy Chicken & Tomato Pasta Bake with Mozzarella

ingredients.swap: Scatter the basil over one portion only, or serve it on the side.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and put a large pan of salted water on to boil. Finely chop the onion and garlic. Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into two thin pieces. Season with half the mixed herbs, salt and pepper.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken for 3–4 min each side until golden and cooked through with no pink. Move to a board, rest for a few minutes, then cut into strips.

steps.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining oil and the onion to the same pan. Cook for 5 min until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 min. Add the passata, the remaining herbs and a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 min until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, cook the penne for 2 min less than the pack says, so it doesn't go soft in the oven. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

steps.title: Assemble the bake
steps.text: Stir the pasta, chicken, parmesan and a splash of the cooking water into the sauce. Tip into a medium baking dish and level the top. Scatter over the torn mozzarella and the cheddar.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.text: Bake on the middle shelf for 20 min, until golden and bubbling at the edges. Leave to settle for 2 min, then scatter with basil leaves (optional) and serve.

title: Cheesy Tuna & Sweetcorn Pasta Bake with Broccoli

ingredients.swap: Cook the sweetcorn in a small pan of boiling water for 3 min instead of with the pasta, and stir it into one half of the dish only before topping with cheese.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Put a large pan of salted water on to boil and heat the grill to medium-high. Cut the broccoli into small florets, halve the cherry tomatoes and grate the cheddar. Drain the tuna.

steps.title: Cook the pasta and veg
steps.text: Cook the penne according to the pack, adding the broccoli and sweetcorn for the last 3 min. Scoop out a small mugful of the cooking water, then drain everything in a colander.

steps.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 min. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 3–4 min, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon.

steps.title: Mix the bake
steps.text: Take the sauce off the heat and stir in two-thirds of the cheddar, the mustard and some salt and pepper. Fold in the pasta, veg and tuna, adding a splash of cooking water if it's stiff. Gently stir in half the tomatoes.

steps.title: Grill and serve
steps.text: Tip into a heatproof baking dish. Scatter over the remaining cheddar, the parmesan (optional) and the rest of the tomatoes. Grill for 5–6 min until golden and bubbling, then serve straight away.

title: Oven-Baked Chicken & Bacon Risotto with Spinach

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and boil the kettle. Finely chop the onion and bacon and grate the garlic. Cut the chicken into 2cm chunks. Crumble the stock cube into 550ml just-boiled water.

steps.title: Brown the chicken and bacon
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide ovenproof pan or casserole with a lid over a medium-high heat. Fry the chicken and bacon for 5 min, stirring, until golden. Add the onion, turn the heat to medium and cook for 4 min until soft.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Stir in the garlic for 30 sec, then add the risotto rice. Stir for 1–2 min until the edges of the grains look see-through.

steps.title: Bake the risotto
steps.text: Pour in the hot stock, add a good grind of pepper and bring to the boil. Cover with the lid, or tightly with foil, and bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 min. It's ready when the rice is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Take the pan out and stir in the spinach for 1–2 min until wilted. Beat in the butter and most of the parmesan until creamy, adding a splash of hot water if it's thick. Check the chicken is cooked through, taste for salt, and serve with the rest of the parmesan and a squeeze of lemon (optional).

title: Chicken & Chorizo Pasta in a Smoky Tomato Sauce

ingredients.swap: Tear the basil over one portion only at the table.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, slice the pepper and crush the garlic. Cut the chicken breast into bite-size pieces and slice the chorizo into half-moons. Crumble the stock cube into 350ml just-boiled water and stir to dissolve.

steps.title: Fry the chorizo
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan or sauté pan with a lid over a medium-high heat. Add the chorizo and fry for 2–3 min until it releases its red, smoky oil.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken to the chorizo oil with a pinch of salt. Fry for 4–5 min, turning, until golden on all sides. It will finish cooking in the sauce.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4 min, stirring, until starting to soften. Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 30 sec until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the pasta
steps.text: Pour in the chopped tomatoes and stock, then stir in the dried pasta. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on a medium-low heat for 12–15 min, stirring every few minutes. It's ready when the pasta is tender and the chicken is white all the way through; add a splash of water if it looks dry.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in the double cream (optional) and bubble for 1 min until glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Spoon into bowls and top with the parmesan and basil (both optional).

title: Tomato & Mozzarella Gnocchi Bake with Basil

ingredients.swap: Stir half the basil into the sauce as normal, and scatter the rest over one portion only at the end.
Sprinkle the chilli flakes over one portion only.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the grill to high and boil a full kettle. Crush the garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes. Tear the mozzarella into small pieces and grate the parmesan. Pick the basil leaves.

steps.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Fry the garlic for 1 min until fragrant but not brown. Add the passata, cherry tomatoes and half the basil, torn, then season. Simmer for 8 min until the tomatoes soften and the sauce thickens slightly.

steps.title: Cook the gnocchi
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, pour the kettle into a large saucepan over a high heat and add a pinch of salt. Cook the gnocchi for 2–3 min until they float to the top. Drain well.

steps.title: Combine in the dish
steps.text: Stir the spinach into the sauce for 1 min until wilted. Fold in the drained gnocchi so every piece is coated. Tip into a medium ovenproof dish and spread out evenly.

steps.title: Grill until bubbling
steps.text: Scatter the mozzarella and parmesan over the top. Grill for 5–7 min until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden in patches.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Leave to stand for 2 min. Scatter over the remaining basil and the chilli flakes (optional), then spoon into bowls.

title: Crunchy Beef Tacos with Cheddar & Soured Cream

ingredients.swap: Leave the lettuce off one plate.
Put the jalapeños in a small bowl so they can be added to one portion only.
Scatter the coriander over one portion only at the table.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (or as the shell packet says). Finely chop the onion and crush the garlic. In a small bowl, mix the cumin, smoked paprika, ground coriander, chilli powder and mixed herbs. Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes, grate the cheddar, then slice the avocado (optional) and cut the lime into wedges.

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Add the beef mince and fry for 5–6 min, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until well browned with no pink left.

steps.title: Season the mince
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and add the onion. Cook for 4 min until soft. Stir in the garlic, spice mix and tomato purée for 1 min. Pour in 75ml water and simmer for 3–4 min until the mince is saucy but not runny, then season with salt.

steps.title: Warm the shells
steps.text: While the mince simmers, stand the taco shells on a baking tray. Warm them in the oven for 3–4 min until hot and extra crisp.

steps.title: Build the tacos
steps.text: Spoon the mince into the warm shells. Top with lettuce, tomato, cheddar and a spoonful of soured cream, then the avocado (optional). Add jalapeños and coriander (both optional) and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.

title: Veggie Bean Chilli with Roasted Sweet Potato & Rice

ingredients.swap: Chop the coriander and scatter it over one portion only at the table.

steps.title: Prep the veg
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Peel the sweet potato and cut into 2cm chunks. Chop the onion and pepper and slice the garlic. Drain and rinse both tins of beans. Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs clear.

steps.title: Roast the sweet potato
steps.text: Toss the sweet potato on a baking tray with 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, the cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Roast for 25–30 min, turning halfway, until golden and tender.

steps.title: Soften the veg
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6–8 min, stirring, until soft and lightly coloured. Add the garlic for the last minute.

steps.title: Simmer the chilli
steps.text: Stir in the remaining 1 tsp cumin, the smoked paprika, chilli powder and tomato purée and cook for 1 min. Add the chopped tomatoes, both tins of beans and 100ml water. Bring to the boil, then simmer on a medium-low heat for 20–25 min until thick, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: About 15 min before the chilli is ready, put the rice in a small saucepan with 300ml boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on a low heat for 10 min. Take off the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 5 min.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir the roasted sweet potato into the chilli and squeeze in half the lime. Season with salt and pepper. Serve over the rice with the soured cream and coriander (both optional), and the other lime half cut into wedges.

title: Steak Fajitas with Smashed Avocado & Soured Cream

ingredients.swap: Scatter the coriander over one portion only at the table.
Serve the jalapeños in a small bowl so they can be added to one portion only.

steps.title: Marinate the steak
steps.text: Trim any thick fat from the steak and slice it thinly (about 5mm) against the grain. In a bowl, mix half the lime juice with the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt. Toss the steak in it and leave for 10 min while you prep.

steps.title: Prep the veg and toppings
steps.text: Slice the peppers and onion into thin strips. Mash the avocado with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt. Grate the cheddar.

steps.title: Cook the peppers
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the peppers and onion for 6–8 min, stirring now and then, until soft and charred at the edges. Tip into a bowl and cover to keep warm.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Put the pan back on a high heat with the remaining 1 tsp oil. Add half the steak in a single layer and cook for 1–2 min, stirring, until browned outside and just pink inside. Repeat with the rest, then return the peppers to the pan and toss for 30 sec.

steps.title: Warm the wraps
steps.text: Wipe out a second frying pan and set it over a medium heat. Warm the wraps one at a time for about 20 sec per side until soft and pliable.

steps.title: Fill and serve
steps.text: Pile the steak and peppers into the wraps. Top with smashed avocado, soured cream and cheddar. Add coriander and jalapeños (both optional), then roll up.

title: Chicken Shish Kebabs with Buttery Rice & Garlic Yogurt

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the salad without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Sprinkle the chilli flakes over one portion only.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Grate the half onion into a bowl and crush in 2 garlic cloves. Stir in 3 tbsp of the yogurt, the tomato purée, smoked paprika, turmeric and 1 tsp salt. Add the chicken chunks and coat well. Chill for at least 20 min, or up to 24 hours. If using wooden skewers, soak 4 in cold water.

steps.title: Make the salad and sauce
steps.text: Dice the cucumber, quarter the tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion. Toss together with the lemon juice, 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt. Mix the remaining yogurt with the last garlic clove and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Thread the skewers
steps.text: Heat the grill to high. Thread the chicken and pepper pieces alternately onto 4 skewers. Lay them on a foil-lined baking tray brushed with the remaining 1 tsp oil.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat and fry the orzo for 2–3 min until golden. Stir in the rice, 300ml boiling water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on a low heat for 10 min, then rest off the heat, lid on, for 5 min.

steps.title: Grill the kebabs
steps.text: While the rice cooks, grill the skewers for 10–12 min, turning halfway, until charred at the edges. Check a thick piece: the chicken should be white all the way through with no pink.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fluff the rice with a fork. Serve the kebabs on the rice with the salad and garlic yogurt alongside. Sprinkle with chilli flakes (optional) and add lemon wedges for squeezing.

title: Chicken Gyros with Tzatziki & Crispy Chips

ingredients.swap: Make one portion of the tzatziki without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. In a bowl, mix 2 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp of the yogurt, the mixed herbs, ½ tsp salt and plenty of pepper. Add the chicken thighs and coat well. Leave for at least 20 min, or up to 24 hours in the fridge.

steps.title: Roast the chips
steps.text: Cut the potatoes (skin on) into 1cm chips. Toss on a large baking tray with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt, spread out in one layer. Roast for 35–40 min, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Make the tzatziki
steps.text: Halve the cucumber lengthways. Scoop the seeds out of one half, coarsely grate it and squeeze out the liquid with your hands. Mix with the remaining yogurt, the last garlic clove, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Chill until needed.

steps.title: Make the salad
steps.text: Dice the other cucumber half and the cherry tomatoes. Finely chop the red onion. Toss together with any remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: About 15 min before the chips are ready, heat the remaining 1 tsp oil in a large frying pan or griddle pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 4–5 min each side until golden and cooked through, with no pink inside. Rest on a board for 5 min, then slice.

steps.title: Warm the pittas and serve
steps.text: Warm the pittas in the toaster or oven for 1–2 min, then split them open. Fill with salad, sliced chicken and a big spoonful of tzatziki. Serve the chips on the side, or tuck a few inside Greek-style.

title: Lamb Moussaka with Potatoes & Golden Cheese Sauce

ingredients.t: ½ lamb or beef cube in 100ml water

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan and line 2 baking trays with baking paper. Slice the aubergine into 5mm rounds. Peel the potatoes and slice them 5mm thick. Finely chop the onion, crush the garlic and grate the parmesan. Crumble the half stock cube into 100ml just-boiled water.

steps.title: Roast the aubergine
steps.text: Brush the aubergine slices on both sides with the oil and season with salt. Lay them on the trays in a single layer. Roast for 20 min, turning halfway, until soft and golden.

steps.title: Make the lamb sauce
steps.text: Meanwhile, heat a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the lamb mince for 5 min, breaking it up, until browned, then spoon off most of the fat. Add the onion and cook for 5 min until soft. Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, cumin, mixed herbs and tomato purée for 1 min. Add the chopped tomatoes and stock and simmer for 25 min until thick, not watery.

steps.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps.text: While the sauce simmers, cook the potato slices in a pan of boiling salted water for 5–6 min until just tender at the edges. Drain and leave to steam dry. Turn the oven down to 180°C fan.

steps.title: Make the white sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium-low heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 min. Gradually whisk in the milk, then simmer for 4–5 min, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Take off the heat, stir in half the parmesan, season, cool for 2 min, then beat in the egg.

steps.title: Layer the moussaka
steps.text: Lay the potato slices over the base of a medium ovenproof dish (about 20 x 20cm). Top with half the aubergine, all the lamb sauce, then the rest of the aubergine. Pour over the white sauce and scatter with the remaining parmesan.

steps.title: Bake and rest
steps.text: Bake for 30–35 min until deep golden and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 10 min before cutting so the layers hold together.

title: Feta-Stuffed Greek Lamb Burgers with Tzatziki & Wedges

ingredients.swap: Leave the feta out of one burger and crumble it over the other at the table instead.
Make one portion of the tzatziki without the cucumber, or serve the cucumber on the side.
Leave the lemons off one plate.
Make one portion of the tzatziki without the lettuce, or serve the lettuce on the side.
Make one portion of the tzatziki without the tomatoes, or serve the tomatoes on the side.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan. Cut the potatoes (skin on) into wedges. Finely chop half the red onion and thinly slice the rest. Coarsely grate the cucumber and squeeze out the liquid. Crush the garlic, separate the lettuce leaves and slice the tomatoes.

steps.title: Roast the wedges
steps.text: Toss the wedges on a baking tray with 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mixed herbs and a pinch of salt. Roast for 30–35 min, turning halfway, until golden and crisp at the edges.

steps.title: Shape the burgers
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the lamb mince with the chopped red onion, panko, Worcestershire sauce, the remaining 1 tsp mixed herbs, a pinch of salt and plenty of pepper. Divide in two and flatten each into a disc. Put 30g feta in the centre of each, fold the meat around it to seal, then shape into patties about 2cm thick. Chill until needed.

steps.title: Make the tzatziki
steps.text: Mix the yogurt with the grated cucumber, garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Cut the rest of the lemon into wedges.

steps.title: Cook the burgers
steps.text: About 15 min before the wedges are ready, heat the remaining 1 tsp oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the burgers for 5–6 min each side until browned and cooked through, with no pink in the middle. Rest for 2 min. Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan for 1 min.

steps.title: Build and serve
steps.text: Layer lettuce and tomato on the bun bases, then add the burgers, a spoonful of tzatziki and the sliced red onion. Add the bun lids and serve with the wedges and lemon wedges on the side.
